title: Fire Emblem: The Binding Blade
subtitle: Roy leads an army across Elibe
summary: Fire Emblem: The Binding Blade is Intelligent Systems' Game Boy Advance tactical role-playing game following Roy and his growing army through a war in Elibe. Story scenes introduce the next conflict before the player moves individual soldiers across a grid-based battlefield. The first handheld entry in the series also gave Roy an adventure of his own after his appearance in Super Smash Bros. Melee. Its campaign depends on developing a particular group of characters, making the outcome of a map important both to the wider story and to the people available for the next battle.
body: Fire Emblem: The Binding Blade is Intelligent Systems' Game Boy Advance tactical role-playing game following Roy and his growing army through a war in Elibe. Story scenes introduce the next conflict before the player moves individual soldiers across a grid-based battlefield. The first handheld entry in the series also gave Roy an adventure of his own after his appearance in Super Smash Bros. Melee. Its campaign depends on developing a particular group of characters, making the outcome of a map important both to the wider story and to the people available for the next battle.

Units have different weapons, movement ranges and responsibilities, requiring the player to consider which opponent each character should face. The weapon triangle gives axes, lances and swords advantages over one another, adding another relationship to the choice of position. Equipment also has a limited number of uses, so preparing an attack involves the condition of the weapon as well as the strength of its bearer. A successful turn coordinates several decisions, placing one unit where it can contribute without leaving another exposed to an enemy response that the group cannot safely absorb.

Characters gain experience through battle, allowing the army's strengths to develop over the campaign. Losing a unit can remove that individual from the remaining journey, giving an otherwise successful map a lasting cost. Recruiting and protecting people therefore matter alongside reaching the immediate objective. The Binding Blade uses the continuing roster to connect its separate battlefields: a capable veteran represents earlier decisions and successful encounters, while another recruit offers possibilities that still need to be developed. The larger strategy includes deciding whose growth can be supported without taking an unnecessary risk.
story_headings: Roy leads an army across Elibe
The campaign remembers a costly decision
